characterization_methods.key_findings: Polycrystalline material shows a coarse grain structure with grain sizes of the order of 1 mm; the as-cast material contained no second phases.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The pure iron used as the 0 at.% Al reference was prepared by electron-beam remelting; specimens were taken with perpendicular orientations in the original ingot.

processing_steps.method: as-cast (used without any subsequent heat treatment)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Tested in the as-cast condition; the as-cast material contained no second phases. No subsequent heat treatment was applied (in contrast to the annealed/quenched Fe-Al monocrystal specimens).

processing_steps.method: electrostatic discharge machining, mechanical polishing, ultrasonic cleaning in acetone, and surface grinding before compression testing
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Specimens were cut by electrostatic discharge machining, mechanically polished and cleansed by ultrasound in acetone (except the monocrystals); the surfaces of the 5x5x10 mm3 compression specimens were cleansed by grinding.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Yield stress determined as 0.2% proof stress in compression with total straining of at least 5%; yield stress of pure iron obtained by averaging the data for 3 rather coarse-grained specimens (perpendicular orientations in the original ingot); yield-stress data were reproducible to within 3% at most

average_grain_size.value: coarse-grained (grain size of the order of 1 mm for the polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys)

microstructure_list.region: bulk (original ingot; specimens with perpendicular orientations)

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline pure iron, coarse-grained (rather coarse-grained specimens), as-cast condition with no second phases

unmapped_findings: Pure iron corresponds to the polycrystalline alloy with nominal 0 at.% Al in Table 1; its real Al content was not determined (n.d.) and its carbon content is 100 wt.ppm, with Si and other impurities not listed.

The yield stress of pure iron was obtained by averaging the data for 3 rather coarse-grained specimens (with perpendicular orientations in the original ingot) of iron prepared by electron-beam remelting (b0032).

Pure iron provides the 0 at.% Al anchor point of the linear yield-stress vs Al-content relationship; the interpolating straight lines indicate a yield-stress increase of 21 MPa per at.% Al at 10^-2 s^-1 and 23 MPa per at.% Al at 10^-4 s^-1 (b0032).

The overall solid-solution hardening coefficient of the polycrystalline as-cast alloys with 0-18 at.% Al is about 2.2 GPa, which is not sensitive to deformation rate or temperature; the linear increase is described by Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys (b0058).
In Fig. 3 at 0 at.% Al the open circle (10^-2 s^-1) lies on the 100 MPa gridline and the filled circle (10^-4 s^-1) sits between the 0 and 100 MPa lines (figure_003).

Pure iron was tested in compression (both strain rates) at room temperature as part of the composition-dependent yield-stress study; no tensile ductility, hardness or fracture data are reported specifically for the pure iron specimen.
